input.rationale: This exploration reduces the two recorded gaps for candidate 0a6d446a083a42cf91e99726f577eaea. Gap 2 (recovery path), closed by a new in-package Go test run: after a transient LogStore.StoreLogs failure made AddVoter(phantom) install a two-voter latest while the durable log still ends at index 2, the node was shut down and a fresh Raft was constructed from the same durable store and snapshot store. Observed (CA_EVENT restart_after_failed_durable_write): servers_before_restart lists the real voter plus phantom/phantom-addr/Voter, while servers_after_restart lists exactly one voter and became_leader_after=true (commit index 3). So the durable log, not the published configuration, is the recovered truth, and a restart is a working recovery path. The same run also bounded the running-process behaviour: after the failed change the node stayed Candidate with ever_leader_in_window=false over 141 samples because quorum_size_live=2 equals one unreachable voter plus itself (CA_EVENT progress_after_failed_durable_write); source reasoning explains the absence of self-repair, since the only running paths that revert r.configurations.latest to the committed value are the appendEntries truncation branch (raft.go:1530) and installSnapshot (raft.go:1937), and both require a leader while no leader can be elected against an unreachable voter. Gap 1 (no-error reachability), answered as a sourced negative result plus a success-path control: the success control CA_EVENT config_persist_success_control shows AddVoter error <nil>, getlog_at_assigned_idx_err <nil> for the assigned index 4 and durable_last_index_after=4, i.e. the published two-voter configuration has a durable counterpart; that fixes the comparing value (the divergence does not appear when the write succeeds). Enumerating every publishing site shows appendConfigurationEntry (raft.go:1203-1240 -> raft.go:1237) is the only site that can install a configuration absent from the log: appendEntries truncation reverts to the committed configuration (raft.go:1530), processConfigurationLogEntry installs the configuration of an entry that was just stored or read from the log (raft.go:1588-1598), installSnapshot installs the received snapshot's configuration (raft.go:1937), and startup restore installs the snapshot's configuration (api.go:664). No no-error route to the divergence was found. Retained evidence for this exploration is the clean-copy execution the controller associates with the submitted harness; the failure is injected at the real LogStore boundary (explicitly supplied precondition, not produced by real producers), and the phantom voter's unreachability is supplied by the harness's lack of a route to phantom-addr.
input.question: For the accepted claim claim-config-publish-requires-durable-append: is the published-vs-durable configuration divergence reachable without any LogStore error, and does only a restart repair the authority context after a failed membership change?

selections.rationale: Sourced suspicion: appendConfigurationEntry (raft.go:1203-1241) calls dispatchLogs first, then unconditionally executes r.setLatestConfiguration(configuration, index), r.leaderState.commitment.setConfiguration(configuration) and r.startStopReplication(). dispatchLogs (raft.go:1244-1279) assigns applyLog.log.Index before StoreLogs and returns early only on its own error path, so future.Index() is still nonzero and the new configuration is published even though nothing was durably stored. The live configuration is the authority input for quorumSize()/checkLeaderLease() (raft.go:1036-1101), requestVote/requestPreVote admission (raft.go:1603-1813) and the election-start gate in runFollower (raft.go:158-260), so publishing an unpersisted configuration can change the node's own quorum requirement. The harness supplies a transient LogStore.StoreLogs failure at the real boundary (storage failure injection) on an otherwise healthy single-voter cluster that had just committed index 3. Observed (CA_EVENT config_publish_after_failed_durable_write): AddVoter returned the store error; the assigned log index 4 is absent from durable storage (getlog_at_assigned_idx_err=log not found, durable_last_index_after=3, raft_last_index=3); yet the node's published configuration now lists two voters (the real one plus phantom/phantom-addr). Observed (CA_EVENT progress_after_failed_durable_write): after the failure the node never regains leadership over 141 samples/1.5s (state=Candidate, ever_leader_in_window=false) because voters_in_live_configuration=2 sets quorum_size_live=2 while only 1 voter is reachable, so electSelf/preElectSelf can never reach the needed tally. This is conditional evidence: it establishes what the fixed code did for an explicitly supplied transient storage failure; the failure itself is injected, not produced by real producers here. A separate observation from the same run: Raft.GetConfiguration().Index() (api.go:897-906 building configurations{latest:...} without latestIndex, returned by configurationsFuture.Index() in future.go:267-270) reports 0 for this two-voter configuration (config_index_after=0), so the published index of the live authority context is not observable and cannot be used as the prevIndex guard that AddVoter/RemoveServer accept. Unresolved discriminators: whether an equivalent divergence is reachable without storage failure; whether a restart (durable log lacks the entry) is the only recovery path; and the exact set of store-failure timings (pre- vs post-StoreLogs) that produce the divergence.

Sourced contract violation in the membership/authority transition path. configurations.latest is documented as the latest configuration in the log/snapshot (configuration.go:254-265) and is the sole authority input for the leader's quorum: quorumSize() (raft.go:1086-1094) counts voters from r.configurations.latest, and commitment.setConfiguration (commitment.go:53-64) rebuilds the match-index voter set from the new configuration. appendConfigurationEntry (raft.go:1203-1240) must therefore only install a configuration that exists in the log, but it calls dispatchLogs first and then unconditionally runs setLatestConfiguration / commitment.setConfiguration / startStopReplication. dispatchLogs (raft.go:1244-1283) assigns applyLog.log.Index before StoreLogs and returns after responding the error, so future.Index() is still nonzero when the write failed. A retained clean-copy execution (exploration 19c98425e4d9482cadcf9bfa3e4f7a85) supplied one transient LogStore.StoreLogs failure on a single-voter cluster that had committed index 3 and observed: AddVoter returned the store error; the assigned index 4 is absent from durable storage (durable last index 3, raft last index 3); the published configuration lists a phantom second voter; and the node then never regains leadership over 142 samples (state Candidate, quorum 2, reachable voters 1), i.e. progress stops until restart. This claim is the sourced requirement, not the experiment; the harness and events are retained with the exploration.
